objective.name: sandbox.dsl.foreach.continue.partial
objective.description: Build a collection, then iterate with on_error=continue so one failing item does not abort the whole loop.

#root.role: Build one deterministic batch, deliberately fail one iteration through a matter read error, continue the other iterations, and aggregate only the successful terminal payloads.

effects.partial_loop_success: Successful iterations remain aggregated even when one iteration fails.
effects.local_iteration_failure: One iteration intentionally produces a local matter read error.

transformation_contract.morphing: A local DSL request becomes one partial aggregate after a bounded loop continues past one failed iteration and preserves the successful items.
invariants: Exactly one iteration is designed to fail through a missing local matter read while the others terminate through sandbox.echo.
The loop keeps on_error=continue semantics, so failed iterations are omitted from the final items array instead of aborting the whole flow.
success: The terminal payload exposes only the successful item payloads in order, excluding the failed iteration.
For count=3 in the N7 fixture, the resulting items array contains the first and third built messages only.
failure: The flow fails if the batch cannot be built before iteration starts.
The flow also fails if a non-tolerated loop error occurs outside the single continued iteration path.
notes: This scenario exists to validate partial success semantics for >for_each with on_error=continue.
The intentional failure path uses matter.read so the continued error remains observable and deterministic.
